features.t: Azure Backup for AKS
x: A backup vault, AKS backup policy and backup instance are real ARM resources validated like the RP (see azure.aks.backup in aks.json); no volume snapshot is taken from a running cluster.

features.t: Diagnose and solve problems, Tasks
x: Diagnose and solve problems is real: detectors (core/azure_diagnose_core.py) are computed from the resource's live configuration, child resources and recorded operations; there is no platform telemetry behind a simulator, so none reads invented metrics and there is no AI troubleshooter.

features.t: Capacity gauge
x: The Capacity gauge is derived from the gateway's own recorded request rate over the last 60 s against a nominal requests-per-second per unit of the service tier (azure_apim_gateway_core); it is a simulator throughput model, not CPU or memory of a real gateway.

features.t: Wiring a new service to Log Analytics, Application Insights or Defender for APIs at create time
x: The create wizard's Monitor + secure tab really creates the diagnostic setting (Log Analytics), the Application Insights logger and the Defender for APIs plan; the wiring is created together with the service request, not as one atomic deployment, so a failure part-way leaves the service created.

features.t: Create wizard: linked database and secure unique default hostname
x: The Create Web App wizard provisions a linked Azure SQL or Cosmos DB database, writes the connection string, links Application Insights and honours 'secure unique default hostname' (azure.appservices.webapp.createdatabase); PostgreSQL, MySQL and Redis options are not offered.

features.t: Browse and Scale blades for a single container
x: The Browse blade lists a container's items through the Cosmos data plane and the Scale blade charts request-unit consumption from the account's metrics and sets throughput; the standalone container-level Settings blade is a Data Explorer tab.

features.t: BitLocker recovery-key escrow (informationProtection/bitlocker/recoveryKeys)
x: Escrow store only: keys are generated in the real recovery-password format and each read is audited, but no disk is encrypted and nothing is unlocked by a key. Escrow is triggered through a Vyomi-specific POST, because real escrow comes from the Windows OS client.

features.t: Entra grid toolbar actions
x: Bulk operations run on the real Graph $batch endpoint and per-user MFA state is stored and enforced by the password grant; Export Data Settings, Columns, Preview features and Got feedback remain unmodelled.

features.t: Diagnose and solve problems, Tasks
x: Diagnose and solve problems is real: detectors (core/azure_diagnose_core.py) are computed from the resource's live configuration, child resources and recorded operations; there is no platform telemetry behind a simulator, so none reads invented metrics and there is no AI troubleshooter.

features.t: Manage deleted keys and secrets (recover / purge)
x: Soft-deleted keys and secrets are kept (with deletedDate and a 90-day scheduledPurgeDate) and can be listed, read, recovered or purged over the native /deletedkeys and /deletedsecrets REST. The retention clock is informational: nothing is purged automatically when scheduledPurgeDate passes, and re-creating a deleted name overwrites it instead of returning 409. Deleted certificates are not modelled.

features.t: Enable access for VMs, ARM template deployment and disk encryption
x: The Access configuration blade stores enabledForDeployment, enabledForDiskEncryption and enabledForTemplateDeployment on the vault through ARM and reads them back; no VM, template-deployment or disk-encryption flow consults them, so the flags are configuration only.

features.t: Integrations (Stream Analytics, Fabric mirroring, Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI)
x: Fabric mirroring and the Power Platform (Power BI, Power Apps, Power Automate) are separate Microsoft SaaS products that Vyomi does not run; the blades say so. Data Sync is real (azure.sql.data_sync) and the connection string on the Connection strings blade is what those tools would use.

features.t: Database watcher: live engine sampling
x: Samples (size, per-table row counts, measured statement latency/failures) are taken from the real engine each time the console asks and kept in a bounded in-memory ring; there is no background collector, no Data Explorer/Kusto store, no KQL dashboards and no CPU/IO/wait metrics because the engine has no resource governor.

features.t: Diagnose and solve problems, Tasks, external SQL client
x: Diagnose and solve problems is real: detectors (core/azure_diagnose_core.py) are computed from the resource's live configuration, child resources and recorded operations; there is no platform telemetry behind a simulator, so none reads invented metrics and there is no AI troubleshooter. Available on the database blade.

features.t: Always Encrypted
x: Always Encrypted (column master keys and client-side column encryption) is not modelled; Transparent data encryption is a separate, real-as-config page (azure.sql.transparent_data_encryption).

features.t: Private endpoint connections
x: The storage account's Networking > Private endpoint connections tab is real: Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints targeting the account write a privateEndpointConnections child on it, approve/reject/delete flow back to the endpoint, and the create wizard can add an endpoint inline (azure.vnets.private_endpoints). No packet is routed: the endpoint does not change how the account's data plane is reached.

features.t: Force delete, Resource group insights, Tasks
x: Force delete of VMs and scale sets inside a group, Resource group insights and Tasks (Azure Automation / Logic Apps) are not modelled; plain delete of the group and of its resources is real (azure.resourcegroups.rg.crud).

features.t: Container Registry support and troubleshooting pages
x: Diagnose and solve problems is real: detectors (core/azure_diagnose_core.py) are computed from the resource's live configuration, child resources and recorded operations; there is no platform telemetry behind a simulator, so none reads invented metrics and there is no AI troubleshooter.

features.t: Data Migration: real container-to-container and JSON-to-container copy
x: Copies documents through the data-plane write path (system properties regenerated, change feed and cosmosDBTrigger functions see every row) with query filter, field rename/drop/set, conflict policy and dry run. It is not the Azure Database Migration Service: no external sources (MongoDB, SQL Server, CSV files from disk) and no live/continuous sync.

features.t: Add Azure Function: creates a real cosmosDBTrigger function in a Function App
x: The function runs through the Function App's sandboxed Python invoke path on each data-plane write; the template handler is fixed and other languages/runtimes are not executed.

features.t: Power BI integration
x: Power BI is a separate Microsoft SaaS product; the blade offers no connector. Use Data Explorer or the SDK.

features.t: Sync to other databases: hub-to-member row sync
x: Run on demand (no schedule), one direction per run, primary-key upsert with hub-wins or skip conflict handling and optional delete propagation, between databases of this simulator. Not SQL Data Sync agents: no sync groups on a schedule, no on-premises members, no schema change tracking triggers.
